Inglewood, California
  October 1, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
  Tuesday, October 1, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
  the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
  Authority, Finance Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at
  the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority
  Secretary/Finance Authority/Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority  Chairman/Finance  Authority
  Chairman/Parking  Authority  Chairman/Joint
  Powers Authority Chairman Butts, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority  Members/Finance  Authority
  Members/Parking  Authority  Members/Joint
  Powers Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor  Agency/Housing  Authority/Finance  Authority/Parking
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

180  COMMENDATION – RECOGNIZING CALIFORNIA CITIES CLEAN
  AIR DAY. The City Council presented Coalition for Clean Air with a
  commendation recognizing their outstanding efforts set forth with Clean Air Day.
  Chris Chavez, Representative for the Coalition for Clean Air, thanked the City
  Council for recognizing their organization.

  COMMENTS – SENATOR BRADFORD REGARDING SENATE BILL
  206. Senator Bradford commented that Governor Newsome has signed Senate
  Bill 206 into law. Sen. Bradford explained that this bill is landmark legislation
  that affords college athletes the right to monetize their name, likeness, and image
  should the athlete decides. He also stressed that what this bill really does is go to
  incentivize the young athlete to stay in college longer, and possibly graduate since
  they don’t have to be lured by the financial temptation of professional sports.
  Sen. Bradford also stated that while 3% of undergraduates are Afro-American,
  they make up 50 % of football and basketball teams who generate revenue for the
  teams, so this will help the Afro-American culture. Sen. Bradford stated that this
  is the Civil Rights issue of the day.

  Mayor Butts stated that this bill is great because high profile athletes always make
  the decision whether they will stay in college or not, and if they get hurt while
  playing professional ball, and not have a professional career, it will still allow the
  athlete to be compensated.

  Sen. Bradford affirmed and mentioned that SB 206 will also protect the female
  athlete.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency

  were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded
  by Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member
  Padilla that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated September 27, 2019, in the amount of
  $6,236,000.98, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency

  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority

  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letter from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  rejection of the claim filed by Gerald Hutchinson for alleged vehicle damage in
  accordance with Government Code Section 913.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member
  Dotson, and carried that the above listed claims be denied.

  NOSSAMAN, LLP. Staff report dated October 1, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment One to Agreement No. 19-155 with

  legal services provided to the City.

  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to

  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council

  vote:

  and
  Noes: None.

 168  ORDINANCE NO. 20-01 INTRODUCED – AMENDING INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPETER 3 (MOTOR VEHICLES AND TRAFFIC)

  92(e)(PARKING METER RATES). Staff report dated October 1, 2019, was

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member

  roll call vote:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA

  SPACE
